key_insight: A cognitively grounded small language model framework can generate more realistic SUD patient dialogue by aligning responses with latent patient states such as beliefs, coping strategies, and readiness to change.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support safer, more deployable counseling dialogue systems in resource-constrained healthcare settings where large models are costly, slow, or harder to govern.
method: Two-stage pipeline: cognitive component detection followed by cognitive component-aligned dialogue generation.
Training combines knowledge distillation, human-annotation preference optimization, and attention-guided reward shaping.
Targets alignment between patient history, counselor questions, and clinically meaningful cognitive responses.
evidence_signal: Across automatic metrics (BERTScore, ROUGE, METEOR, BLEU) and LLM-as-judge hit-metrics against human and teacher references, the cognitively informed SLM outperformed generic instruction-tuned and mental-health-specific baselines, especially for open-ended cognitive components.
watch_item: Performance gains come from abstract evaluation signals rather than direct clinical outcome testing, so real-world safety, robustness, and user impact still need validation.
paper_title: Multi-Objective Aligned Small Language Model Framework for SUD Patient Dialogue Generation
